about.title: Personal Injury Help in Greenfield, California
about.longDescription: Greenfield sits along Oak Avenue and El Camino Real, with Elm Avenue and Walnut Avenue rounding out the corridors that carry most of the town's daily traffic. Public records show 25 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, leaving 27 people hurt — a reminder that even a small city sees its share of serious wrecks. Whether it happened at a busy intersection on El Camino Real or on a quieter stretch of Elm Avenue, the aftermath of a crash can leave you dealing with medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls you didn't ask for. We provide a free case review to help injured people in Greenfield understand what happened and explore your options. There's no cost to talk, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You don't have to figure this out alone or guess at deadlines. A short conversation can help you understand where things stand and what steps, if any, make sense next for your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can mean losing the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover a share of damages. We can help sort out how fault might actually be divided in your case.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit the amount you can seek for non-economic harm like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life. That's worth discussing with someone who understands how these claims are valued.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee to hire representation. We only get paid if your case results in a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Greenfield?
items.answer: In most California injury cases you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved — say a city vehicle or a road maintenance issue — that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover damages even if you were partially at fault. Your recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of responsibility, not eliminated entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Greenfield?
items.answer: Public crash records show that reported collisions tend to happen more often on Oak Avenue, El Camino Real, Elm Avenue, and Walnut Avenue, with activity peaking on Saturdays between about 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply the corridors and times where public records show more reported collisions, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get a case review?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we help injured people in Greenfield and throughout Monterey County evaluate their situation at no cost.

items.question: Will I owe money if my case doesn't result in a settlement?
items.answer: We work on a contingency basis, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. If there's no recovery, you typically owe no attorney fees for the work done on your case.
